# Practitioner Academy Proposal: Tamarack Instruments

**To:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel
**Re:** Two-day Practitioner Academy, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. The Client is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. Its stated AI maturity is Piloting, with three AI use cases at different stages:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

In June 2026, an internal audit finding recorded that the Client holds no inventory of AI systems. The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected to start next year, although the start date is not fixed. Your objective is plain: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

## 2. Why Hands-On Practitioner Capability Fits Now

The Client has one system in deployment and one in pilot, with a fixed production target. Governance needs to be built by the people who will run it, working on real systems rather than abstractions.

The Practitioner Academy places seven roles in the same working sessions for two days:
- General Counsel
- CISO
- Head of Quality
- Head of Data
- German plant manager
- Two internal auditors

These participants build first versions of the artifacts the audit finding and the Q2 2027 objective call for. The program is a starting point for capability. It does not by itself close the audit finding, and it does not promise any certification or audit outcome.

The Client holds an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and an ISO 9001 quality management system. Which existing procedures, records or controls under those systems can be reused for AI governance is Unknown. This proposal does not assume any. Participants will identify candidate connection points for the Client to confirm.

The program teaches three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human.

## 3. Running Worked Examples

We propose two running examples across both days:

1. **AI visual inspection.** This example is tied directly to your Q2 2027 objective. It also exercises the works council constraint.
2. **The customer service chatbot.** This is the deployed system. It exercises GDPR and the requirement that customer data stays in the EU.

AI sales forecasting enters the inventory as a planned system. It serves as the intake example, showing how a system is governed before it is built.

**Confidentiality handling:**
- All exercises use sanitized analogs. Session transcripts, inspection scenarios and forecasting inputs will be written for the program, so no customer data enters the sessions or the repositories.
- Visual inspection exercises involve no production staff and use no production imagery or worker data.
- Any workflow element that would touch production staff is recorded as an open item for German works council consultation before it progresses.
- Where the Client's working copies of the repositories will be hosted is Unknown. This will be agreed before Day 1.

## 4. Curriculum Spine

Participants work directly in the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). Each day runs as four 90-minute working sessions. Exact file paths for each module and pattern will be confirmed in the pre-work packet.

### Day 1: GRC Workbook

| Session | Exercise | Module or Pattern | Artifact Produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Governance structures | The facilitator tells *The Turtle and the Phoenix* from the [facilitation kit](https://github.com/rolldabones/AI-Governance-Academy/blob/main/the-turtle-and-the-phoenix.md), then runs the kit's twenty-minute closing exercise. Participants then map decision rights for both worked examples. Owners not yet named are rendered Unknown. | GRC Workbook, governance structures module, bridged through the kit's handle map | Draft decision-rights map |
| 2. Inventory and classification | Enter the chatbot, visual inspection and sales forecasting systems. Draft classification rationale against the EU AI Act and GDPR. | GRC Workbook, AI system inventories and classification module | Started AI system inventory with draft classifications |
| 3. Risk and impact assessment | Assess candidate risks for both worked examples, including data residency for the chatbot and the works council dependency for visual inspection. | GRC Workbook, risk and impact assessments module | Draft risk register entries and draft impact assessments |
| 4. Policies and procedures | Draft an AI intake procedure using sales forecasting as the test case. List candidate ISMS and QMS connection points for confirmation. | GRC Workbook, policies and operating procedures module | Draft intake procedure and policy outline |

### Day 2: Slow AI Kitchen and Assurance

| Session | Exercise | Module or Pattern | Artifact Produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5. Governed prompting | Specify governed prompts and refusal boundaries for the chatbot, using sanitized transcripts. | Slow AI Kitchen, governed prompting pattern | Governed prompt specification |
| 6. Workflow design | Design the visual inspection workflow and the chatbot escalation workflow end to end. | Slow AI Kitchen, practical AI workflow design pattern | Two governed workflows |
| 7. Human oversight | Set oversight, override and sign-off points. Draft go-live acceptance criteria using The Definition of Done (https://github.com/rolldabones/definition-of-done). | Slow AI Kitchen, human oversight and accountability pattern | Oversight map and draft acceptance criteria |
| 8. Evidence and audit readiness | Build an evidence index for each artifact. Draft a board-level summary using AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). | GRC Workbook, evidence collection and audit readiness | Evidence index and draft board summary |

## 5. Deliverables

By the close of Day 2, the Client will hold:
- A started AI system inventory covering three systems.
- Draft risk register entries for both worked examples.
- At least two governed workflows: visual inspection and chatbot escalation.
- A governed prompt specification.
- An oversight map with draft acceptance criteria.
- An evidence index.

Each artifact is a working draft. Who owns finishing each one is Unknown and will be agreed during Session 8.

## 6. Logistics and Price

- **Format:** Two days, live virtual. Each day has four 90-minute working sessions.
- **Dates:** Unknown.
- **Session times:** Unknown. These will be set once participant locations are confirmed.
- **Video platform:** Unknown.
- **Pre-work:** A short pre-work packet will be issued before Day 1.
- **Price:** US$12,500. This sits within the stated approved budget of up to US$80,000 for this fiscal year.

## 7. Next Step

Your decision is expected by 15 December 2026. On approval, we propose a 30-minute scheduling call to confirm:
- Dates and session times.
- Participant names against the seven stated roles.
- Repository hosting.
- The sanitized analog approach for customer data and production scenarios.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: The Session 1 cell bundles the fable, the kit's twenty-minute closing exercise and decision-rights mapping, and gives one module and one artifact for the whole row. I read the row-level module and artifact as covering all of it. A stricter scorer could say the closing exercise has no separately named artifact and fail item 4.

Session 4 lists 'candidate ISMS and QMS connection points' alongside the intake procedure, but the artifact cell names only 'Draft intake procedure and policy outline'. I treated the list as part of the policy outline.
Session 8 pairs the evidence exercise with a GRC Workbook module although Day 2 is the Slow AI Kitchen day. The system prompt describes Day 2 as 'plus assurance', so I accepted it.

Client facts that go slightly beyond the Profile Block wording: 'fixed production target', and the audit finding stated as 'the Client holds no inventory'. I judged both to be restatements of the stated objective and the June 2026 audit finding. Under the v1.14.3 guidance the works council dependency for visual inspection follows from the stated constraint and is not a new fact. The ISO 27001 and ISO 9001 reuse is rendered Unknown. Another scorer could read 'fixed' as overreach.
The text says 'seven roles' but lists six roles (two internal auditors) across seven people. This is a counting slip, not a Client fact, and is not a checklist item or fail indicator.
score.reasoning: All seven checklist items are met. The output is a single Mode A proposal that keeps the eight-session spine and the 2-day, US$12,500 constants. Every exercise row names a repository module or pattern and an artifact. Worked examples come from AI_USE_CASES, and confidentiality is handled explicitly through sanitized analogs. The closing line is present. No Client facts beyond Part 2 appear: unknown items (dates, platform, hosting, artifact owners, ISMS and QMS reuse) are rendered Unknown. The stated constraints are applied without inventing incumbent registers, owners or system states. The judgment calls above are minor and none triggers a fail indicator.
